title: Production of Genetically Engineered Golden Syrian Hamsters by Pronuclear Injection of the CRISPR/Cas9 Complex
protocol: Synthesize sgRNAs following the in vitro transcription procedures described in the manual of synthesis kit.
Mix 2 µg of Cas9 with 1 µg of sgRNA and incubate the mix at room temperature for 10 - 15 min.
Make a working solution at the concentration of 100 ng/µL Cas9 and 50 ng/µL sgRNA with 10 mM TE buffer (RNase free).
Anesthetize males by intraperitoneal injection of ketamine/xylazine with a dose of 40 mg/kg (ketamine) and 10 mg/kg (xylazine).
Confirm anesthesia by lack of a pedal reflex (toe pinch).
Lay the sedated hamster in dorsal recumbency on a dry tissue paper.
Rinse the abdomen with three rounds of antiseptic treatments using alternating surgical scrub solutions between 70% alcohol and povidone-iodine.
Make a vertical incision with surgical scissors starting 1.5 cm cranial to the prepuce extending 1 cm to each side from mid line.
Incise the skin, subcutaneous tissue, and linea alba to access the peritoneal space.
Apply gentle pressure to the caudal aspect of the scrotum to force the testes and fat tissue out.
Grasp the vas deferens gently with forceps and carefully separate the blood vessel from the vas with a second set of forceps.
Hold the vas deferens with forceps to form a loop.
Heat the tip of another forceps in flame until it is red, and then use it to remove the loop of the vas deferens.
Insert fat tissue and testes back into the abdomen.
Remove the vas deferens on the opposing side using the same procedures.
Suture the musculature first followed by suturing the skin.
Place the animal on a warm pad in a cage for 30 min until the animal recovers.
Observe the animal until it resumes normal activity.
Superovulate sexually mature females (>6 weeks) on the first day of estrous by IP injection of PMSG dissolved in PBS as 50 IU/mL between 9 - 12 AM.
Place females 80 - 84 h after injection of PMSG (Day 4, 6 - 8 PM) in cages with males for mating.
Prepare pseudopregnant females by mating sexually mature females on Day 4 of estrous with vasectomized males.
Prepare culture medium (HECM-9) as described previously in McKiernan and Bavister.
One day prior to PN injection, prepare zygote handling dishes (25 μl/drop) and a PN injection drop (100 μl) in the lid of a 35 mm dish with HECM-9.
Cover the medium drops with mineral oil.
Balance medium in an incubator overnight under conditions: 37.5 °C, 10% CO2, 5% O2, 85% N2 and 100% humidity.
On the day scheduled for PN injection, prepare embryo flushing dishes (1 dish/donor hamster) with HECM-9.
Store all dishes in the incubator until use.
Euthanize superovulated hamsters with CO2.
Isolate oviduct.
Place a euthanized female hamster in dorsal recumbency on a surgical drape or tissue paper.
Prepare the abdomen with a 70% ethanol spray.
Hold skin and abdominal muscle layer at the midline and make an incision.
Incise the peritoneum to expose the abdominal organs.
Grasp one of the uterine horns with a fine forceps and retract the tissue from the abdomen.
Separate the uterus from the mesometrium and fat tissue.
Make a cut between the oviduct and ovary and a second cut adjacent to the junction of the oviduct and uterus, including a small part of uterus.
Place the two oviducts in the same flush dish.
Grasp the side of uterine horn with a #5 Dumont forceps and insert a homemade needle into the lumen of the oviduct from the infundibular end.
Flush the oviduct with 300 - 400 µL of HECM-9 medium under the dissection microscope.
Collect the zygotes immediately.
Wash the collected zygotes twice with HECM-9 medium in a handling dish.
Place the denuded zygotes in an incubator at 37.5 °C, 10% CO2, 5% O2, 85% N2 and 100% humidity immediately after collection to minimize exposure to light.
Thaw the Cas9/sgRNA RNP on ice.
Maintain the complex on ice during the entire PN injection process.
Load the injection needles with Cas9/sgRNA RNP solution immediately before the injection experiments.
Place the rear end of the injection needles into the tube containing the Cas9/sgRNA RNP solution.
Allow the Cas9/sgRNA RNP solution to fill the needle by capillary action.
Prepare the injection dish and needles.
Fill the holder pipette with mineral oil to within ~3 mm of the bend of the holder needle.
Place the holder in the microinjector with the tip of the needle horizontal to the bottom of the dish.
Fill the tip of the needle with medium by suction.
Set the injection needle at a 10 - 15° angle opposite to holder.
Identify a zygote and apply a fine suction with the holder needle.
Penetrate the zona and male pronuclei (3 o'clock position) with the injection needle.
Withdraw the injection needle quickly once the pronucleus swells.
Transfer zygotes to pseudopregnant hamsters.
Anesthetize a pseudopregnant hamster.
Lay the anesthetized pseudopregnant hamster on a surgical drape or dry tissue paper in ventral recumbency.
Apply eye lubricants to the eyes of the animal to prevent dryness.
Cover the head with a cloth or paper to protect the eyes from light.
Shave a 4 cm x 4 cm skin area on each side of the body.
Apply povidone-iodine scrub three times on each side.
Apply 70% ethanol scrub three times on each side.
Make a 2 cm vertical incision 2 cm caudal to the last rib on each side.
Grasp the fat pad with forceps and pull gently until the oviduct and uterus are visible.
Clamp the fat pad with hemostats and reflect it dorsally over the spine.
Position the reproductive tract so that the uterine tube can be penetrated with a 30 gauge needle for embryo transfer.
Wash injected zygotes with HECM-9 in a new dish.
Load 10 - 15 zygotes into a glass pipette (diameter: ~150 - 200 µm).
Arrange the zygotes as a chain of pearls followed by several air bubbles.
Insert the pipette into the open penetrated uterine tube and gently blow to transfer the zygotes to the oviduct.
Release the fat pad and return the tissue to the abdomen.
Transfer approximately the same number (10 - 15) of injected embryos to another oviduct tract using the same process.
Suture the musculature in 2 layers.
Suture the skin in 2 layers.
Administer Buprenorphine-HCl (0.5 mg/kg) subcutaneously as post-op analgesia.
Place the hamster on a warm pad for recovery after surgery.
Return the cage to the animal room when the hamster is fully recovered from anesthesia.
Administer post-op analgesics again six hours later.
